notes: This HARA is a library-level self-assessment for github.com/SoundMatt/go-SOMEIP, an ASIL-B (see .fusa.json) SOME/IP protocol implementation. Severity/Exposure/Controllability are estimated for a representative automotive zonal-Ethernet integration; a library alone is not an item, so an integrating system MUST re-derive its own item-level HARA rather than adopt these ratings directly. ASIL values here are a conservative ceiling used to scope this library's own safety requirements and mitigations (RELAY spec x-FuSa lifecycle, spec §20.4).

operationalSituations.description: Normal operation: reliable local Ethernet segment, conformant peers, nominal load.
Degraded network: packet loss, reordering, or duplication on UDP; a slow or unresponsive peer.

Concurrent application usage: multiple goroutines calling Subscribe/Unsubscribe/Call/Emit on the same Service/Server/Subscription simultaneously, as the package's own concurrency-safety doc comments promise.

hazards.description: A malformed or wrong-protocol-version SOME/IP frame (truncated, inconsistent Length field, or non-0x01 ProtocolVersion) is silently accepted and processed as if valid, causing the application to act on corrupted or attacker-influenced data.

The native Message ↔ relay.Message conversion (Message.ToMessage / FromMessage) silently drops or corrupts header semantics (ClientID, SessionID, MessageType, ReturnCode, InterfaceVersion) when a message is bridged through RELAY tooling (relay crossbar, relay interop, convert), causing the receiving application to act on incorrect message semantics without any error being raised.

An event subscription (udp.Service.Subscribe) silently fails to register with the server, or concurrent Subscribe/Unsubscribe calls corrupt shared subscriber state (data race / send-on-closed-channel), so that safety-relevant event notifications never reach the subscribing application without any error being surfaced (go-SOMEIP#47, go-SOMEIP#48).

A SOME/IP request that should receive a timely response never completes (unreachable server, dropped datagram, or a hung handler) and the calling goroutine blocks indefinitely instead of failing over to a safe state within a bounded time.

safetyGoals.description: Reject any inbound frame that is structurally malformed or carries an unsupported ProtocolVersion before it reaches application code.
safetyGoals.safeState: codec.Decode returns ErrShortFrame/ErrLengthMismatch and Message.Validate returns ErrWrongProtocolVersion; the caller never sees a Message built from the malformed bytes.

safetyGoals.description: Message.ToMessage/FromMessage MUST be a lossless round trip for every mandatory SOME/IP header field.
safetyGoals.safeState: Every header field not carried in the ID is restored byte-for-byte from Meta; verified by TestMessageRoundTripLossless and by relay interop (which requires byte-identical relay.Message output for the shared golden vector).

safetyGoals.description: Subscribe MUST register the subscriber with the server (or fail loudly) before returning success, and concurrent Subscribe/Unsubscribe/dispatch MUST NOT race or panic.
safetyGoals.safeState: Service.Subscribe sends a Subscribe entry and returns an error if it cannot be sent; Server.RegisterSubscriber/UnregisterSubscriber and the mutex-protected copy-on-write subscriber list make dispatchFrame, Subscribe, and Unsubscribe mutually exclusive; verified under -race by TestUDPSubscribeEmit, TestUDPUnsubscribeStopsDelivery, and TestUDPSubscribeUnsubscribeRace.

safetyGoals.description: Every blocking call MUST have a bounded, caller-controlled deadline.
safetyGoals.safeState: Service.Call returns ErrTimeout once ServiceConfig.Timeout (default 5s) elapses, or ctx.Err() if the caller's context is cancelled; the caller is never blocked indefinitely.
